### ⚪ Migration Queensland has updated its skilled visa overview page with clearer onshore and offshore pathway labels and minor text refinements.
_Migration Queensland – Skilled visas_

**What changed**
- Pathway titles now explicitly specify onshore/offshore status (e.g. 'Skilled workers living outside Australia (offshore)' and 'Skilled workers living in Queensland (onshore)').
- 'Building and construction workers' pathway title updated to 'Building and construction workers in Queensland (onshore)'.
- 'Small business owners in regional Queensland' pathway title updated to include '(onshore, subclass 491 only)'.
- Minor editorial adjustments made to introductory guidance and visa subclass descriptions.

**Who it affects:** No one – wording or layout change only.

**What to do:** Nothing – for information.

[Official page](https://migration.qld.gov.au/visa-options/skilled-visas) · [Exact wording changes](https://github.com/Rafidk9/immi-watch/blob/main/changes/2026-10/20261030-1256_qld-skilled.md) · severity: **low**

### ⚪ VETASSESS Melbourne Head Office will be closed on Tuesday 3 November 2026 for the Melbourne Cup public holiday.
_VETASSESS – news & updates_

**What changed**
- VETASSESS Melbourne Head Office will be closed on Tuesday 3 November 2026.
- Closure is due to the Melbourne Cup Public Holiday.
- The notice for scheduled portal maintenance during August 2026 has been removed.

**Who it affects:** Applicants and agents contacting or awaiting assessment processing from VETASSESS on 3 November 2026.

**What to do:** Nothing – for information. Factor the single-day office closure into communication and processing timelines.

[Official page](https://www.vetassess.com.au/news) · [Exact wording changes](https://github.com/Rafidk9/immi-watch/blob/main/changes/2026-10/20261030-1640_vetassess-news.md) · severity: **low**

### ⚪ Home Affairs has launched a compliance campaign assessing smart glasses against mandatory cyber security standards under the Cyber Security Act 2024.
_Home Affairs – Portfolio news (incl. OMARA, ministerial)_

**What changed**
- Under the Cyber Security Act 2024, consumer-grade smart devices must meet mandatory baseline security standards.
- The Department of Home Affairs’ Technology Assessment and Regulation Office has begun assessing smart glasses compliance.
- Retailers of smart glasses have been asked to inform their suppliers and manufacturers of applicable Australian regulatory requirements.
- The announcement relates solely to consumer device cyber security regulation and has no bearing on immigration, visas, or education programs.

**Who it affects:** Retailers, suppliers, and manufacturers of smart glasses (no impact on visa applicants or migration clients).

**What to do:** Nothing – for information.

[Official page](https://www.homeaffairs.gov.au/News-subsite/Pages/2026-Oct/smart-glasses-compliance-in-focus.aspx) · [Exact wording changes](https://github.com/Rafidk9/immi-watch/blob/main/changes/2026-10/20261030-1841_ha-news-portfolio.md) · severity: **low**

### ⚪ Migration Queensland has made minor editorial wording updates to its skilled visas overview page.
_Migration Queensland – Skilled visas_

**What changed**
- Introductory text changed from stating Queensland nominates for '2 skilled visa subclasses' to 'nominates skilled workers for the following skilled visa subclasses'.
- Eligibility criteria prompt updated to refer to the pathway that best matches your 'circumstances' instead of 'situation'.

**Who it affects:** No one – wording or layout change only

**What to do:** Nothing – for information

[Official page](https://migration.qld.gov.au/visa-options/skilled-visas) · [Exact wording changes](https://github.com/Rafidk9/immi-watch/blob/main/changes/2026-10/20261030-1841_qld-skilled.md) · severity: **low**

### ⚪ WA State Nominated Migration Program updates occupation search filter text and corrects 14 October invitation round data
_Migration WA – State Nominated Migration Program_

**What changed**
- Corrected typographical error stating invitations 'were issues' to 'were issued' on 14 October for priority trade and non-trade occupations
- Corrected location data for subclass 491 invitation round entries: one entry changed from 'Western Australia' to 'Overseas', and another from 'Western Australia' to '-'
- Standardised subclass 190 invitation round location entry from 'WA' to 'Western Australia'
- Minor wording edit to instructions for filtering the eligible occupations list

**Who it affects:** No one – wording and reporting corrections only

**What to do:** Nothing – for information

[Official page](https://migration.wa.gov.au/our-services-support/state-nominated-migration-program) · [Exact wording changes](https://github.com/Rafidk9/immi-watch/blob/main/changes/2026-10/20261030-1841_wa-snmp.md) · severity: **low**
